item.title: General Relativity in Three Lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.22396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that complex general relativity can be formulated directly in terms of three affine lines assigned to each spacetime point. The lines are represented by Pl\"ucker bivectors, and Urbantke's construction applied to the associated two-forms reconstructs the conformal spacetime metric. Starting from the chiral Pleba\'nski action, the simplicity constraints turn the three two-forms into a null internal basis of simple bivectors and thereby into three projective lines. A $3+1$ decomposition then yields a first-order canonical theory whose configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines and whose conjugate variable is a line momentum. The resulting constraint system consists of three internal Gauss constraints, three vector constraints, and one Hamiltonian constraint. A notable feature of the line formulation is that the equation obtained by varying the line momentum is pointwise algebraic after the spatial integrations by parts. Consequently the momentum can be eliminated explicitly wherever the corresponding Legendre map is invertible, giving a second-order action whose only dynamical configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines. The line curvature separates naturally into a cosmological trace and the Weyl matrix of the selected chiral sector. The Legendre map becomes singular on a distinguished null-evolution locus where the spacetime metric remains nondegenerate. There its rank drops from nine to six, giving three algebraic compatibility conditions. We construct a finite invariant partial Legendre transform and a smooth constrained second-order continuation through this locus. This analysis provides a regular framework for regimes in which the evolution direction becomes null and may be useful in the study of near-horizon geometries and related gravitational phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Pawel Nurowski

item.title: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.22767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansion of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose mondromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddle points. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia package Resurgence.jl
item.dc:creator: Samuel Crew, Job Feldbrugge

item.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
item.description: arXiv:2610.23320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlev\'e IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve. We further establish the compatibility of this folding with the associated wave functions and quantum curves. In the Bessel-Clifford example, this yields an explicit relation between the equivariant and folded wave functions and recovers the corresponding quantum curve reduction. These results provide a framework for relating symmetry reductions of integrable systems to folding operations in topological recursion.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Alameddine, Alexander Hock

item.title: Randomness from initial conditions: The challenge of incompleteness
item.description: arXiv:2610.23355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Certain prima facie deterministic theories, notably Bohmian mechanics and kinetic theory, require ``random'' initial conditions in order to achieve their goals. I analyze recent proposals that this idea should be implemented using algorithmic randomness, seen as a mathematical sharpening of the typicality arguments originally used to understand these theories. On the one hand my analysis includes a critique of these arguments and hence a defense of this sharpening. On the other hand, I argue that Chaitin's incompleteness theorems for random sequences make it impossible for a dynamical theory to either process given random initial conditions beyond some finite (but not arbitrary) number of their digits, or else to state such conditions with arbitrary precision without compromising their randomness (these are two sides of the same coin). This challenges the ability of such theories to make any other predictions than those that hold typically in the usual sense of the word (like macroscopic statements), and moves their alleged determinism high up the metaphysical ladder.
item.dc:creator: Klaas Landsman

item.title: Geodesics in Black-Hole Spacetimes: A Qualitative Classification Using Vieta's Formulae
item.description: arXiv:2610.22399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This monograph classifies the geodesics of the Schwarzschild, Kerr and Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes without solving for their turning points. In all three spacetimes, the radial and polar motions are governed by polynomials whose coefficients depend only on the constants of motion, and the qualitative behavior of a geodesic is fixed by the pattern of their roots. We read this pattern directly off the coefficients, using Vieta's formulae together with the discriminant, Descartes' rule of signs, and the values of the polynomials at the horizons and at infinity. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the reciprocals of the radial roots of every non-radial geodesic add up to $1/(2M)$, which gives the third root of a bound orbit in closed form and the separatrix $p=6+2e$. In Kerr spacetime, the signs of the coefficients show that no radially bound orbit has $\varepsilon^2\geq1$ and that vortical geodesics, timelike or null, have no radial turning point; a positive discriminant is necessary but not sufficient for bound motion, and Descartes' rule applied at the event horizon gives the exact criterion. Spherical orbits and their stability, the equatorial ISCO and light rings, and the photon shell follow from the same relations. In Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime, the timelike radial polynomial is a quintic with exactly one negative root, a bound branch requires $\varepsilon^2+\Lambda L^2/3<1$, and both marginally stable circular orbits lie beyond $6M$. Most of these results are known; the aim is to show that a single, elementary algebraic route leads to all of them. The text is meant for graduate students who have taken a first course in general relativity, and each chapter ends with worked examples.
item.dc:creator: Oliver F. Piattella

item.title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.22489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.
item.dc:creator: Kaumudibikash Goswami, Archana Barvar, Manabendra Nath Bera

item.title: No cosmic horizons from a strengthened higher-dimensional strong energy condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.22506v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Time-dependent supergravity compactifications lie beyond the setting of the Gibbons/Maldacena-Nu\~nez no-de Sitter theorem and can even support eternal cosmic acceleration, raising the question of whether they can also produce future cosmic horizons. For general higher-dimensional matter, the strong energy condition alone does not exclude such horizons. Here, we demonstrate that a theory fulfilling a strengthened version of the strong energy condition cannot be compactified down to a lower-dimensional theory able to support a future cosmic horizon. For 10d and 11d supergravities reduced to at least four large spacetime dimensions, this energy condition is fulfilled by the sources that already fulfill the strong energy condition in the higher-dimensional theory. Our assumption on the dimensional reduction is that it is performed on a smooth compact and boundaryless space.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Tonioni

item.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.
item.dc:creator: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin, Ryan Thorngren

item.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Chervov, Ilia Gaiur, Sergey Galkin, Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk, Volodya Rubtsov, Shamil Shakirov

item.title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.22821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|^{\beta}$ on $I_{\theta} := [ - (\log{T})^{\theta},(\log{T})^{\theta}]$, for every $\theta > 0$ and $\beta > 0$. As $\beta$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|\zeta|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $\sigma$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $\beta_{c}(\theta) := 2\sqrt{1 + \theta}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $\beta \leq \beta_{c}(\theta)$, and assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $\beta > \beta_{c}(\theta)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.22823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.
item.dc:creator: Will Cavendish

item.title: Streamwise dispersion with interphase mass transfer through a tube
item.description: arXiv:2610.22963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reactive solute transport in shear flows is of broad importance in chemical engineering, liquid--solid chromatography, and environmental mechanics, particularly in flow reactors and fluidic devices involving interphase mass transfer. Based on the recently developed streamwise dispersion theory for inert solutions (Guan & Chen, 2024, J. Fluid Mech., vol. 980, A33), we present an analytical model for reactive dispersion of chemically active solutes characterized by first-order, irreversible surface reactions. The extension is not a simple perturbation because the reactive boundary destroys mass conservation with streamwise and radial derivatives coupled. The model establishes how the microscopic kinetic reactivity and radial eigenmodes combine to determine a newly defined (effective) local exchange rate. We derive rigorous explicit solutions for the local moments, concentration, and phenomenological transport coefficients at arbitrary reactivity, in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations across all regimes. For tube Poiseuille flows, we reveal pre-asymptotic behaviours including sign-changing radial exchange, reactivity-enhanced drift, reactivity-reduced dispersivity, and non-Gaussian concentration profiles. Small- and large-Damk\"ohler-number asymptotics for the local and global transport coefficients identify the reaction-limited and diffusion-limited regimes, connecting the conservative case to the Dirichlet limit at infinite reactivity. This streamwise perspective could advance our understanding of macroscale transport in chemically active systems.
item.dc:creator: Mingyang Guan, Zhan Wang

item.title: Parity-dependent sublattice structure of local $2\times2$ correlations in domino tilings of the Aztec diamond
item.description: arXiv:2610.22974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study local $2\times2$ correlations in uniformly random domino tilings of the Aztec diamond $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$, a dimer model with frozen corners and a liquid region bounded by the Arctic circle, and compare them with the square chessboard. For every elementary square the probabilities $P_H$ and $P_V$ of the two coverings by a pair of parallel dominoes satisfy $P_H=P_V=P_1P_2+P_3P_4$, where $P_1,\dots,P_4$ are the probabilities of the four surrounding edges. This known identity, a case of Kuo's graphical condensation, reduces the spatial profile of $P_H$ to single-edge probabilities, which we compute exactly from the inverse Kasteleyn matrix for all squares of $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$. The squares form two interleaved sublattices, distinguished by the color of their lower-left cell. The parity of $n$ decides which sublattice dominates near the center: the one containing the central square for odd $n$, and the other one for even $n$. This sign rule holds for the averaged sublattice contrast for all $4\le n\le22$. It also fixes the location of the global maximum of $P_H$, which lies at or next to the center for odd $n$ and several lattice spacings away for even $n$. Within the central sublattice, the preferred square follows a mod-4 pattern that matches the exactly pinned mean height of the center. On the $L\times L$ chessboard the same rule holds with $n$ replaced by the half-width $L/2$, but the contrast is two to six times weaker, the central edge probability never equals $1/4$, and the maxima of $P_H$ are pinned to the corners. The exact $1/4$ values and the interior, parity-selected maxima are therefore features of the Aztec geometry.
item.dc:creator: Chaeyeon Kim, Suhwan Yoo, Jeehoon Choi, Hee Young Kwon, Changyeon Won

item.title: Anticommuting Displacement Operators, Exact Pauli Algebras,and the Singlet State from the Oscillator Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.23264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an explicit construction of a pair of anticommuting Weyl displacement operators for a harmonic oscillator and use bounded functional calculus to obtain exact dichotomic representatives of the Pauli algebra. Two independent oscillators provide commuting Pauli algebras for Alice and Bob. The standard singlet-sector projector, written entirely in terms of these bounded oscillator observables, is then applied to the two-oscillator vacuum. We show explicitly that the projected vacuum has nonzero norm, so its normalization is well defined, has the exact singlet correlations, and reaches the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt2$ for the usual Bell--CHSH settings. We also clarify that the construction generally realizes a singlet sector with multiplicity, rather than selecting a unique vector in the full oscillator Hilbert space, and we compare the construction with the older pseudospin approach to continuous-variable Bell tests.
item.dc:creator: S. P. Sorella

item.title: Anomalies for compact simple Lie groups via $G$-kernels for loop group nets
item.description: arXiv:2610.23321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a compact simply connected simple Lie group and $k \geq 1$. Jump loops give an outer homomorphism $\theta_k$ from $G$ to the outer automorphisms of the local factor of the level-$k$ loop group net, which is the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor. We show that its Sutherland obstruction is $k$ times the positive basic class in $H^3_{\mathrm{Borel}}(G, \mathbb{T}) \cong H^{4}(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ and that $\theta_k$ is faithful, so it is a $G$-kernel. Central elements act by the outer automorphisms of the simple currents. In types A, D, E the level-one class is computed by comparing maximal-torus jump loops with the lattice $\alpha$-induction construction of the companion paper on both current and charged generators, followed by integral degree-four Cartan restriction. Higher levels follow by tensor additivity, and the remaining types by restriction along index-one embeddings into simply laced groups. As a consequence, for every compact simply connected semisimple $G$, every class in $H^4(BG, \mathbb{Z})$ is the obstruction of a $G$-kernel on the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor.
item.dc:creator: Marcel Bischoff, Pradyut Karmakar

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.23329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong

item.title: Spinors, Doppelg\"angers and the Non-Perturbative Classical Double Copy
item.description: arXiv:2610.23384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a geometric and spinorial formulation of the non-perturbative classical double copy between the Corrigan--Fairlie--'t Hooft--Wilczek sector of complexified SU(2) Yang--Mills theory and four-dimensional conformally flat gravity. We identify the gauge potential with the positive-chiral spin connection of the conformally flat metric, establishing an exact relation between the Yang--Mills field strength and the chiral projection of the Riemann tensor. This provides a four-dimensional realisation of the doppelg\"anger viewpoint, in which gauge and gravitational fields arise from different interpretations of common connection data. Within this sector, the sourceless Yang--Mills equations require constant scalar curvature, explaining the shared nonlinear scalar equation and extending the gravitational correspondence from traceless matter to matter with constant energy--momentum trace. By representing adjoint colour indices as symmetric pairs of spinor indices, we derive exact relations mapping the gauge field-strength spinors to the scalar-curvature and trace-free Ricci components of the gravitational curvature. These relations retain nontrivial curvature information despite the vanishing Weyl tensor. We illustrate the construction using anti-de Sitter and de Sitter spacetimes, together with $\mathrm{AdS}_{3}\times\mathbb{R}$ supported by a scalar field, demonstrating the extension to matter with nonzero constant trace
item.dc:creator: Kymani Armstrong-Williams

item.title: Renormalization Group Domain Walls from Phantom Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.23529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories. Using phantom currents, we consider an auxiliary chiral extension linked to the folded ultraviolet--infrared theory by a topological interface. The construction of RG walls then reduces to identifying suitable automorphism-twisted Cardy states in the auxiliary theory. We find two such types of automorphisms: outer automorphisms exchanging identical current algebra factors, as in Gaiotto's construction, and continuous inner automorphisms generated by the zero modes of spin-one phantom currents. In the latter case, the RG domain walls generically admit a continuous defect conformal manifold. We further show that, when an RG flow can be orbifolded to another one, the orbifold may lift defect conformal moduli of the RG brane constructed using inner automorphisms. The two types of RG branes can then be mapped to each other via a topological interface defined by the orbifold. We demonstrate the two types of RG brane construction via various examples of flows between non-unitary minimal models, from parafermions to minimal models, and between generalized parafermions. Many physical observables of the RG walls are computed non-perturbatively, including boundary entropies and spectra, and UV--IR operator mixings. We also find interesting nontrivial boundary monodromy: a closed cycle in the defect conformal moduli space can carry an RG domain wall into other distinct non-trivial conformal interfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jin Chen

item.title: Partially isophase electro-magnetic configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Separation of variables in Schr\"{o}dinger equation allows an infinite-dimensional family of physically distinct field configurations that are dynamically indistinguishable in one selected sector, labeled by a conserved quantum number, while differing in all others. We call such a symmetry a partial isophase symmetry. Two main examples are considered: axially symmetric magnetic backgrounds (a rigid spectral flow of the Fock--Darwin oscillator, purely magnetic isophase families, and a two-channel extension) and a Cartesian slab geometry (magnetic barriers in two-dimensional electron gases, treated in the Appendices). We further discuss the consequences of this symmetry for the inverse spectral problem and consider its quasiclassical counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Andrey M. Pupasov-Maksimov

item.title: Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity
item.description: arXiv:2610.23674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a theory for the plastic shear rate $\dot{\gamma}_i$ on each slip system $i$ of face-centered cubic (FCC) single crystals, by integrating the shear rate contributions $\dot{\gamma}_i(l)$ from dislocation links of length $l$. A generalized Orowan equation expresses $\dot{\gamma}_i(l)$ in terms of the link density $n_i(l)$ and the average link velocity $v_i(l)$. This model accurately reproduces the discrete dislocation dynamics (DDD) shear-rate data for all 12 slip systems across 99 loading orientations. In particular, it explains why the plastic shear rate depends exponentially on the resolved shear stress $\tau_i$, as reported previously, in the absence of any thermally activated mechanism. This dependence arises from the exponential tail of $n_i(l)$ filtered through the threshold-like velocity function $v_i(l)$. Furthermore, $v_i(l)$ is well approximated by a single two-dimensional function $v(\tau_i,l)$ for all these slip systems. The link velocity is therefore governed mainly by $\tau_i$ and $l$, with only a minor effect from the complex interactions between slip systems. These interactions instead manifest themselves mainly through $n_i(l)$. As a demonstration of the effect of the link-length distribution on the slip rate, we show that even when $\tau_i$ is limited to a narrow window, the shear rates still span two orders of magnitude. The supply of long links is therefore the dominant factor controlling slip-system activity, outweighing the direct effect of $\tau_i$ on the link velocity.
item.dc:creator: Hanfeng Zhai, Sh. Akhondzadeh, Ryan B. Sills, Nicolas Bertin, Wei Cai

item.title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.23695v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Hayakawa

item.title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23712v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Brunialti

item.title: MIXSim: A multiclass first order traffic model with composition-dependent dynamics for mixed-autonomy urban networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.23714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a novel multiclass first order macroscopic traffic model for mixed-autonomy in signalized urban networks, called MIXSim. Human driven vehicles (HDVs) and Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) are represented as separate classes while origin-destination information is retained through commodity specific states. The local vehicle class composition and class specific driving behaviour characteristics determine the parameters of a composition-dependent triangular fundamental diagram. At signalized intersections, the composition of movement demand additionally determines the saturation flow rate, while the realized movement flow is constrained by demand, effective green time, and downstream receiving capacity. Numerical experiments investigate different CAV penetration levels and CAV time gaps, together with alternative signal control strategies. The numerical experiments illustrate how changes in CAV penetration and CAV time gap affect network performance under the tested conditions, and demonstrate the use of MIXSim for comparing signal control strategies across different mixed traffic regimes.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Haris, Claudio Roncoli

item.title: Resonance interaction of vector breathers and exotic dynamics in the coupled Hirota equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work presents a systematic theoretical investigation of vector breathers and their nonlinear interactions in the coupled Hirota equation. This model describes the simultaneous propagation of ultrashort optical pulses in optical fibers and contains a key parameter that characterizes the strength of higher-order linear and nonlinear effects, such as third-order dispersion and self-steepening. For the model, we focus on the focusing-focusing case. On a nonzero plane-wave background, we derive explicit expressions for multi-breather solutions of the coupled Hirota equation by the dressing method. For the single-breather solution, by choosing special constant vectors, the vector breathers can be classified into three fundamental types: Type I, Type II, and Type III. We then analyze their characteristic parameters, including spatial localization and group velocity, as well as important special cases such as the Kuznetsov-Ma breathers, Peregrine soliton, and Akhmediev type breathers etc. Through the above analysis, we find that the higher-order effect parameter only modifies the propagation velocity and oscillation period of the breathers, while the resonance conditions remain satisfied: when the wave numbers and frequencies match, inelastic resonant interactions can occur between Type I and Type II breathers, manifesting either as a fusion process (I + II \rightarrow II) or the reverse decay process (III \rightarrow I + II). Furthermore, we present the explicit expression for the two breather solutions of the equation and analyze its rich interaction scenarios, including two breather resonances and elastic collisions, and we point out that the special case of resonance corresponds to the limiting case of merging eigenvalues. Finally, we carry out numerical simulations to verify the accuracy of the obtained solutions.
item.dc:creator: Li-Juan Bo, Xiu-Bin Wang

item.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
item.description: arXiv:2610.23752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.
item.dc:creator: Omar Kidwai, Guillaume Tahar

item.title: Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models
item.description: arXiv:2610.23777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for Ising measures conditioned to have a sufficiently large majority of $+1$ spins. Under a sparse spectral width condition on the interaction matrix, we derive a Poincar\'{e} inequality for the conditioned measures from a magnetization drift condition, and a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality from a stronger, entropy weighted condition. As applications, we obtain approximate posterior sampling in total variation distance for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ synchronization at high enough signal-to-noise ratio using $O(n\log n)$ Glauber updates from a spectral initialization. For ferromagnetic Ising models on random $d$-regular graphs, we prove rapid phase ordering down to inverse temperatures of order $1/d$, extending the temperature range of Gheissari, Sly, and Sohn (2025). Finally, we extend these inequalities to unconditioned Ising measures under an inward drift condition outside the conditioned region. This yields $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature when the external field is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Vasyl Paliy, Youngtak Sohn

item.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing elastic particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.23819v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $\gamma=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size. For $\gamma=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $\gamma\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\gamma=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $\gamma=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.
item.dc:creator: J. Casado-D\'{\i}az, A. R. Hormigo-Molina

item.title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.23823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.
item.dc:creator: Pax Kivimae, Benjamin McKenna

item.title: Uniform restriction lower bounds and nongeodesic common nodal curves in integrable systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.23836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a family of real analytic metrics on the two-torus, for which a fixed embedded nongeodesic circle is a nodal component of infinitely many real Laplace eigenfunctions. The examples address a question asked by Bourgain-Rudnick \cite{BR11}, and give a negative answer to the question asked by Toth-Zelditch \cite{TZ21} and Han \cite{Han}: whether a curve shared by infinitely many nodal sets must be geodesic. To explain the restriction obstruction, we prove uniform $L^2$ lower bounds for joint eigenfunctions of quantum completely integrable (QCI) systems under transverse crossing and isolation of a tangential characteristic branch, then extend to multi-branch setting. The results are used to characterize the possible joint nodal curves in the Liouville tori, narrowing down the choices. Finally, the counterexample realizes one possibility for which cancellation happens exactly on a nongeodesic curve.
item.dc:creator: Xianchao Wu, Xiao Xiao

item.title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
item.description: arXiv:2610.23843v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.
item.dc:creator: Lucas D'Alimonte, Lo\"ic Gassmann

item.title: Mean-Field Dynamics of the Bose-Hubbard Model in High Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2501.05304v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Bose-Hubbard model effectively describes bosons on a lattice with on-site interactions and nearest-neighbour hopping, serving as a foundational framework for understanding strong particle interactions and the superfluid to Mott insulator transition. This paper aims to rigorously establish the validity of a mean-field approximation for the dynamics of quantum systems in high dimension, using the Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice as a case study. We prove a trace norm estimate between the one-lattice-site reduced density of the Schr\"odinger dynamics and the mean-field dynamics in the limit of large dimension. Here, the mean-field approximation is in the hopping amplitude and not in the interaction, leading to a very rich and non-trivial mean-field equation. This mean-field equation does not only describe the condensate, as is the case when the mean-field description comes from a large particle number limit averaging out the interaction, but it allows for a phase transition to a Mott insulator since it contains the full non-trivial interaction. Our work is a rigorous justification of a simple case of the highly successful dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for bosons, which somewhat surprisingly yields many qualitatively correct results in three dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Shahnaz Farhat, Denis P\'erice, S\"oren Petrat

item.title: Kohn-Sham models for encapsulated two-dimensional materials
item.description: arXiv:2606.11785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) models describing the electronic structure of two-dimensional materials placed in a three-dimensional environment, encapsulated between two parallel conducting electrodes. In this geometry, the Dirichlet boundary conditions at the electrodes screen the Coulomb interaction, which becomes effectively short-ranged, of Yukawa type. We prove that some nonlinear Kohn-Sham DFT models are well-posed in this setting, both for periodic materials (such as graphene) and for quasi-periodic materials (such as twisted bilayer graphene and other moir\'e materials for generic incommensurate twist angles).
item.dc:creator: \'Eric Canc\`es, David Gontier, Solal Perrin-Roussel

item.title: Exact Chained-Word Threshold and Monotone-Path Structure in the Even Root-of-Unity Kaleidoscope Yang-Baxter Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2609.39262v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Qiu, Guan, and Yu conjectured that in the even-order Kaleidoscope Yang--Baxter equation every word $\Lambda T^{k_1}\Lambda\cdots T^{k_M}\Lambda$, built from a square-zero matrix $\Lambda$ and integer powers of a shift $T$ of order $N$, vanishes once $M\geq N/2$. We prove this for every even $N\geq4$ and every complex parameter $u$ with $u\neq0$ and $u^N\neq1$, and show that the bound is sharp. For $M=N/2-1$ we determine exactly which words are nonzero; each of them has rank two. After block reduction, the factors associated with the intervening powers of $T$ lower a common flag of length $N/2$ by at least one step. The spectral idempotents of $T$ then give a presentation of the algebra generated by $T$ and $\Lambda$ by paths between levels, in which two paths compose only when the level changes monotonically. This algebra is independent of $u$, has dimension $N^2-N+2$, and is a pullback of two incidence algebras. Its radical is generated by $\Lambda$ and has nilpotency index $N/2+1$, and the algebra has infinite global dimension and infinite representation type. Replacing powers of $T$ by arbitrary functions of $T$ gives exact rank formulas and, for $N\geq6$, rank-one elements in the top radical power. Finally, four conditions on a filtered pair of operators over an arbitrary field recover the threshold and the radical; none of them can be omitted.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Zhiyuan Yao

item.title: Time-dependent integrable quantum field theories with dynamical boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.03870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a general method to construct and solve time-dependent integrable chiral quantum field theories on finite intervals from autonomous scattering and reflection data. Spatial homogeneity forces the spectral labels of right- and left-moving particles to be affine with a common slope, so bulk and boundary couplings sample one spectral trajectory. A complete round trip shifts the spectral labels and gives boundary quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations. The Yang--Baxter and reflection equations provide local consistency, while boundary-qKZ flatness provides global consistency. We reconstruct the local Hamiltonian by Cayley inversion of the bulk and boundary matching matrices. We apply the construction to rational $SU(N)$ scattering with fundamental boundary impurities and to an $O(3)$ model with a spin-$\tfrac12$ impurity. For the $SU(2)$ impurity, we construct explicit boundary-qKZ solutions as lattice sums of off-shell boundary Bethe vectors and recover the static open-chain Bethe equations when the drive rate vanishes
item.dc:creator: Pradip Kattel

item.title: Exponential clustering of bipartite quantum entanglement at arbitrary temperatures
item.description: arXiv:2108.12209v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Macroscopic quantum effects play central roles in the appearance of inexplicable phenomena in low-temperature quantum many-body physics. Such macroscopic quantumness is often evaluated using long-range entanglement, i.e., entanglement in the macroscopic length scale. The long-range entanglement not only characterizes the novel quantum phases but also serves as a critical resource for quantum computation. Thus, the problem that arises is under which conditions can the long-range entanglement be stable even at room temperatures. Here, we show that bi-partite long-range entanglement is unstable at arbitrary temperatures and exponentially decays with distance. Our theorem provides a no-go theorem on the existence of the long-range entanglement. The obtained results are consistent with the existing observations that long-range entanglement at non-zero temperatures can exist in topologically ordered phases, where tripartite correlations are dominant. In the derivation of our result, we introduce a quantum correlation defined by the convex roof of the standard correlation function. We establish an exponential clustering theorem for generic quantum many-body systems for such a quantum correlation at arbitrary temperatures, which yields our main result by relating quantum correlation to quantum entanglement. As a simple application of our analytical techniques, we derived a general limit on the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information and the quantum Fisher information, which will attract significant attention in the field of quantum metrology. Our work reveals novel general aspects of low-temperature quantum physics and sheds light on the characterization of long-range entanglement.
item.dc:creator: Tomotaka Kuwahara, Keiji Saito

item.title: Singularity and regularity of the critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow
item.description: arXiv:2504.06128v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) provides a natural candidate solution to the ill-posed 2D Stochastic Heat Equation with multiplicative space-time white noise. In this paper, we initiate the investigation of the spatial properties of the SHF. We prove that, as a random measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$, it is a.s. singular w.r.t. the Lebesgue measure. This is obtained by probing a "quasi-critical" regime and showing the asymptotic log-normality of the mass assigned to vanishing balls, as the disorder strength is sent to zero at a suitable rate, accompanied by similar results for critical 2D directed polymers. We also describe the regularity of the SHF, showing that it is a.s. H\"older $C^{-\epsilon}$ for any $\epsilon>0$, implying the absence of atoms, and we establish local convergence to zero in the long time limit.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Caravenna, Rongfeng Sun, Nikos Zygouras

item.title: On the pair correlation function of the Sine$_\beta$ process
item.description: arXiv:2509.15446v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Sine$_\beta$ process, the bulk point process scaling limit of beta-ensembles. We provide a representation of its pair correlation function for all $\beta>0$ via a stochastic differential equation, and also via an infinite system of differential equations. We show that the pair correlation function is continuous in $\beta$, and provide estimates for its asymptotic decay. When $\beta=2n$ is an even integer, we characterize the pair correlation function through a linear system of $n$ ordinary differential equations and derive the function's power series expansion. Our results recover the classical explicit formula for the pair correlation function in the $\beta=2$ and $4$ cases. We obtain our results by studying the one-point function of the $\operatorname{HP}_{\beta,\delta}$ process, the point process limit of the circular Jacobi beta-ensemble.
item.dc:creator: Yahui Qu, Benedek Valk\'o

item.title: The three kinds of three-qubit entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2511.07617v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct an important missing piece in the entanglement theory of pure three-qubit states, which is a polynomial measure of W-entanglement. This works in parallel to the three-tangle, which is a polynomial measure of GHZ-entanglement, and to the bipartite concurrence, which is a polynomial measure of bipartite entanglement. We also show that these entanglement measures are ordered, the bipartite measure is larger than the W measure, which is larger than the GHZ measure. It is meaningful then to consider these three types of three-qubit entanglement, which are also ordered, bipartite is weaker than W, which is weaker than GHZ, in parallel to the order of the three kinds of equivalence classes of entangled three-qubit states.
item.dc:creator: Szil\'ard Szalay

item.title: Fluid dynamics as intersection problem
item.description: arXiv:2512.25053v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The main result of the paper is a construction of an infinite-dimensional symplectic manifold, associated with spacetime, its coisotropic submanifold defined as the zero locus of a moment map, and a family of Lagrangian submanifolds determined by the equation of state and the spacetime metric, such that their intersection is precisely the covariant Lichnerowicz--Carter system for a relativistic perfect fluid. On this basis, we clarify the notion of canonical velocity and hydrodynamic invariants, such as the asymptotic Hopf invariant and the Ertel invariant, and obtain a generalization of Kelvin's circulation theorem. We also clarify the relation between the canonical velocity, the four-velocity, and other choices of frames. We point out a five-dimensional origin of the formalism underlying the covariant formulation of hydrodynamics. Our formalism extends naturally to fluids with additional degrees of freedom, including multi-component fluids, charged fluids, and superfluids, and incorporates the chiral anomaly and Onsager quantization. It also suggests a direction of research connecting hydrodynamics to Poisson sigma models and topological field theories. Furthermore, we argue that a similar approach applies to the theory of self-dual fields, such as chiral bosons in 1+1 dimensions, tensor fields of (2,0) theory in 1+5 dimensions, and the 4-form field of type-IIB supergravity in 1+9 dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Nekrasov, Paul Wiegmann

item.title: Failure of the mean-field Hartree approximation for a bosonic many-body system with non-Hermitian Hamiltonian
item.description: arXiv:2601.13038v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mean-field Hartree theory is a central tool for reducing many-body dynamics to an effective one-particle evolution. This approximation has been employed when the Hamiltonian governing the many-body dynamics is not Hermitian. Indeed, non-Hermitian Hamiltonians model particle gain/loss or the evolution of open quantum systems between consecutive quantum jumps. Furthermore, the validity of the Hartree approximation for generic non-Hermitian Hamiltonians lies at the basis of a quantum algorithm for nonlinear differential equations. In this work, we show that this approximation can fail. First, we consider the most general bosonic mean-field Hamiltonian with two-body interactions and we prove that, for non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, the Hartree equation does not capture the correct second time derivative of the one-particle marginal state at $t=0$ in the thermodynamic limit. Then, we analytically solve a model of $N$ bosonic qubits with a purely anti-Hermitian Hamiltonian, compute the limit for $N\to\infty$ of the one-particle marginal state and show that it does not agree with the solution of the non-Hermitian Hartree equation. We further show that there exists an initial condition such that the exact one-particle marginal state undergoes a finite-time transition to a mixed state, a phenomenon that is completely absent in the case of Hermitian Hamiltonians. Finally, we simulate a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian with real spectrum and show that, also in this case, there are initial conditions for which the Hartree equation does not reproduce the correct one-particle marginal state in the limit $N\to\infty$. Our findings challenge the validity of the mean-field Hartree approximation for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, and call for additional conditions for the validity of the mean-field regime to model the dynamics of particle gain and loss and the open-system dynamics in bosonic many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Matias Ginzburg, Simone Rademacher, Giacomo De Palma

item.title: Universality classes, Thermodynamics of Group Entropies, and Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2603.02385v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conventional Boltzmann--Gibbs statistical mechanics successfully describes systems with weak to moderate correlations, in which the number of accessible configurations $W(N)$ grows exponentially with the number of degrees of freedom $N$. However, this framework breaks down for systems for which the effectively occupied configuration space exhibits non-exponential growth. While numerous generalized entropies have been proposed to address this limitation, a coherent link to classical thermodynamic laws has remained elusive. Here, we propose group entropies as a unifying framework, defining universality classes of entropies through the asymptotic scaling of $W(N)$, each yielding an extensive entropy. We show that this approach provides the basis for a consistent thermodynamic formulation beyond the Boltzmann--Gibbs paradigm. In particular, by expressing these entropies in terms of thermodynamic state variables, we demonstrate their consistency with classical thermodynamics, in close analogy to the emergence of the Clausius entropy from the Boltzmann--Gibbs formalism. Focusing on the zeroth thermodynamic law, we identify the empirical temperature and, by using Carath\'{e}odory's formulation of the second law, we derive the associated absolute temperature. As an application, we analyse black-hole thermodynamics using the extensive group entropy class corresponding to stretched-exponential behaviour of $W(N)$ and derive a negative heat capacity, known to be a hallmark property of black holes. This result holds for the stretched-exponential entropies associated with both the Bekenstein--Hawking and Barrow entropy scalings.
item.dc:creator: Henrik Jeldtoft Jensen, Petr Jizba, Piergiulio Tempesta

item.title: Hidden symmetry group for particle orbits (timelike geodesics) in Schwarzschild spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2604.16644v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the timelike geodesic equations in Schwarzschild spacetime, three hidden conserved quantities were found recently, which are analogues of dynamical quantities related to the well-known Laplace--Runge--Lenz (LRL) vector in Newtonian gravity. In particular, the geodesic equations possess an LRL angle, an LRL Killing-vector time and an LRL proper time, each of which is a (piecewise) conserved quantity for all timelike geodesics. The present work provides a natural symmetry interpretation for these three quantities by applying Noether's theorem in reverse to the geodesic Lagrangian. This yields three new (hidden) LRL symmetry transformations. Unlike the Killing symmetries, which constitute point transformations on the geodesic configuration variables and close without the use of the geodesic equations, the new symmetries are dynamical transformations which essentially involve the geodesic momenta variables and close only on solutions of the geodesic equations. The commutator structure of the LRL symmetries is shown to depend on whether a geodesic is bounded or not, and horizon-crossing or not, while their physical meaning is connected to their action on the geodesic energy and angular momentum. Together with the Killing symmetries and re-parameterization symmetries of the geodesics Lagrangian, they generate the complete Noether symmetry group of the timelike geodesic equations.
item.dc:creator: Stephen C. Anco, Mahdieh Gol Bashmani Moghadam

item.title: Separability from Multipartite Measures
item.description: arXiv:2605.02097v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that multi-invariants provide necessary and sufficient criteria for full separability in finite-dimensional multipartite systems. For tripartite three-qubit states, the third-order negativity gives an exact criterion for full separability for both pure and mixed states. We then extend the framework to four-qubit pure states, whose full characterization requires eighteen independent real parameters. We identify eighteen independent entanglement measures, consisting of six bipartite, eight tripartite, and four quadripartite measures, with the third-order negativity serving as a key separability criterion. Finally, we generalize the construction to multipartite qudit systems and discuss an application to conformal field theory.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Te Ma, Ma-Ke Yuan

item.title: A generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2606.15174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a generalized long-wave limit method for constructing higher-order (degenerate) lump solutions of $(2+1)$-dimensional integrable systems. Starting from the multi-soliton tau function, we introduce wavenumber rescalings, spectral perturbations, and higher-order phase modulations in a single small parameter, and choose their coefficients so that the lower-order Taylor coefficients vanish. Applying this framework to the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili I equation, we explicitly derive second-order two- and three-lump solutions as well as third-order three-, four-, five-, and six-lump solutions. The long-time asymptotics of the peak positions and amplitudes describe anomalous scattering of these degenerate lump solutions. Extensions to hybrid higher-order lump solutions associated with multiple distinct spectral parameters are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: Holonomies and Boundary Symmetries in the Discrete BF Formulation of Carroll Dilaton Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.25499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a discrete realization of two-dimensional Carroll dilaton gravity based on a BF-type gauge structure with holonomy variables on lattice links. The bulk theory remains topological, while the physical dynamics is encoded in boundary degrees of freedom. Imposing admissible boundary conditions, we derive the asymptotic symmetry structure directly at the lattice level. The least restrictive conditions yield an affine extension of the Carroll algebra, while additional constraints reduce the symmetry to a conformal sector governed by a discrete Virasoro-type algebra. In the continuum limit, the lattice symmetry structure reproduces the expected affine Carroll algebra together with its conformal reduction. The construction therefore provides the ultra-relativistic counterpart of discrete Jackiw-Teitelboim(JT) gravity.
item.dc:creator: H. T. \"Ozer, Ayt\"ul Filiz

item.title: A UV-Finite Refinement of the Ryu-Takayanagi Relation in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2606.27915v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a refined Ryu--Takayanagi (RT) relation in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ using \emph{relative entropy} as the central object, in place of the ultraviolet-divergent von Neumann entanglement entropy. Adapting Hollands' exact result for the chiral relative entropy to a diamond region, we express the boundary relative entropy between the vacuum and a coherent state as a Schwarzian functional, which the Fefferman--Graham dictionary identifies with the asymptotic data of a Ba\~nados geometry; the rigidity of three-dimensional gravity promotes this boundary identification to the bulk. To linear order in the metric perturbation, the relative entropy then equals the variation of the RT geodesic length divided by $4G_N$. The construction rests only on the Bisognano--Wichmann/Borchers theorem and the holographic dictionary, giving a UV-finite, operator-algebraic counterpart to the RT relation.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Dorau, Albert Much, Leonardo Sangaletti, Rainer Verch

item.title: Morse Bridge between Planar Kepler and Hyperbolic Landau Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.01778v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A common Morse Hamiltonian bridges the planar Kepler--Coulomb and hyperbolic Landau systems, linking flat electric dynamics to curved magnetic dynamics. A radial Liouville transformation with coupling-constant metamorphosis maps the separated Kepler problem to the Morse system, while fixed-horocyclic-momentum reduction maps the hyperbolic Landau problem to the same system. In a common normalization, the Coulomb coupling is the signed product of the magnetic field and conserved horocyclic momentum, while the quantum Landau reduction has the universal half-density shift $1/4$. Beyond this shared reduction, we construct a direct classical orbit map on the regular nonradial sectors for all signs of the Kepler energy. It maps the Landau height to a scaled inverse Kepler radius, Kepler ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas to magnetic circles, horocycles and hypercycles, and Hamilton's hodograph affinely to the Landau carrier circle. The reduced Kepler symplectic form and the Binet-selected complex structure determine a Poincar\'e K\"ahler metric. Its nondegenerate Binet orbits have constant geodesic curvature of magnitude equal to the inverse eccentricity, while zero coupling gives geodesics. The orbit map identifies this metric isometrically with the Poincar\'e configuration-space metric of the hyperbolic Landau problem. Composing the quantum Liouville maps eliminates the Morse wavefunction and yields an exact weighted intertwining identity between the radial Kepler and horocyclic Landau operator pencils. At distinguished half-integer magnetic fields, the angular-momentum grading of a fixed Kepler shell is reorganized into the finite reduced Landau tower and its threshold endpoint. These exact correspondences hold in the stated reduced sectors despite the unitary inequivalence of the complete parent systems.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail S. Plyushchay

item.title: Uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the 2D Coulomb gas at the diffusive temperature scale
item.description: arXiv:2608.24863v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $N\ge2$ and $\beta>0$, consider the canonical 2D Coulomb gas ensemble \begin{equation} \mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,\beta}(Z) =\mathsf{Z}_{N,\beta}^{-1}e^{-\beta|Z|^2/2} \prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^{\beta/N}\mathrm{d} Z \qquad\text{on }\mathbb{C}^N. \end{equation} The factor $N^{-1}$ in the pair exponent places the ensemble at the diffusive, or high-temperature, scale. We prove that, for every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$, this Gibbs measure satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality (LSI) on the closed Dirichlet-form domain generated by collision-free compactly supported smooth functions, with a positive constant independent of $N$. The LSI constant may be chosen uniformly when $\beta$ ranges over a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. A second main result establishes Poincar\'e and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for planar Gaussian measures weighted by finite products of positive powers of distances to points, with constants depending only on the total variance of the underlying Gaussian measure and the total exponent, not on the number or locations of the points. To prove the full labeled Poincar\'e inequality, we decompose variance into permutation-invariant and label-dependent parts, controlled respectively by a weighted $\bar\partial$ estimate and by relative-coordinate conditioning with random transpositions; separately, one-site logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, a conditional entropy inequality, and a repulsive partition estimate give a defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. Rothaus tightening combines the resulting full labeled Poincar\'e inequality with the defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The two main theorems on their stated closed form domains and all results used in their formal proofs, including those from the literature, have been formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Rosenzweig

item.title: Bogomol'nyi equations for Kruglov strings
item.description: arXiv:2609.08111v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct the Bogomol'nyi equations for Abelian gauge--Higgs vortices in which the Maxwell gauge sector is replaced by Kruglov nonlinear electrodynamics, a power-law family that interpolates between Maxwell theory, Born--Infeld electrodynamics, and exponential electrodynamics, characterized by a dimensionless exponent $\sigma$. Using the stressless method, we derive a pair of first-order equations directly from the vanishing of the spatial stress tensor, without assuming the Higgs potential \textit{a priori}. For generic $\sigma$, the gauge and Higgs sectors are coupled through an implicit algebraic relation. We therefore introduce a constitutive map $\Phi(Y;\sigma)$ and analyze its monotonicity and range to determine the conditions for a smooth admissible Bogomol'nyi branch. For $\sigma>1/2$, the constitutive map is strictly monotonic and unbounded, whereas for $0<\sigma<1/2$ it possesses a finite maximum; the marginal case $\sigma=1/2$ is bounded. These properties yield explicit bounds on the nonlinear parameter $\beta$ for the latter cases. We further obtain closed-form constitutive relations, BPS potentials, and gauge-field equations for six representative values of $\sigma$, spanning linear, quadratic, and cubic algebraic structures. The corresponding vortex profiles are then computed numerically. The resulting BPS string tension is purely topological, $\mu_{\rm BPS}=2\pi n$, independent of both $\sigma$ and $\beta$.
item.dc:creator: I. Prasetyo, U. Ubaydillah, H. S. Ramadhan

item.title: Autonomous self-harmonic drift in Langevin dynamics causes a compaction of underlying domain for the density of Stochastic Localization
item.description: arXiv:2609.36232v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Our recent research on Langevin dynamics with self-harmonic drift and classical spins has revealed a strong connection to ``Stochastic Localization," a concept attracting attention in the fields of mathematical geometry and data science. Roughly speaking, the former can be viewed as a version of the latter in which the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space - the domain of the probability distribution function appearing in the latter - is ``compactified'' to the surface of an $n$-dimensional sphere. By comparing the two frameworks, we argue that this compactification is a consequence of requiring the drift to be autonomous. The relationship between the two approaches may expand the scope of Stochastic Localization.
item.dc:creator: Ken Sekimoto

item.title: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
item.description: arXiv:2610.11664v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/\lambda$, where $\lambda\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/\lambda)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $\Sigma_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $\Sigma_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.
item.dc:creator: Sergey N. Solodukhin

item.title: Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane, with a proof formalized in Lean
item.description: arXiv:2610.13100v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.
item.dc:creator: Tejasvi Singh Tomar

item.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
item.description: arXiv:2610.15006v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a non-unital partial symmetric operad (combination restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.
item.dc:creator: Xuexing Lu

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16107v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and replace the construction of the exceptional set by a direct exclusion: we use finite boundary charts for seven of the eight diagrams that can carry an unbounded four-product, and an exhaustive order census for Diagram 5. We derive the necessary mass conditions where needed and show that no germ with an unbounded four-product lies on a curve of normalized central configurations through a positive configuration. Five diagrams are excluded for all complex germs, two on curves through real configurations, and one on curves through positive configurations. Parts of the argument are computer-assisted: exact algebra, interval arithmetic and exact linear programming.
